title: Psychological tactics (intimidation, urgency, authority, scarcity)
goal_html: Students learn to name the psychological tactic(s) behind a message and justify a defensive response. Ties to LO 1.1.A (identify indicators) and 1.1.B (explain how tactics influence victims).
steps_html:
1. Each pair opens the simulation and works through the message stream, agreeing on the tactic tag(s) for each before submitting. They must reach the target score.
  2. For any message they got wrong, they write one sentence explaining why the tactic works psychologically (what feeling it engineers).
  3. Pairs draft one original message of their own that stacks at least two tactics, then trade with another pair to classify.
collaborate_html: Assign roles: one partner is the "attacker" (defends why their crafted message is convincing), the other is the "analyst" (names the tactics and the defense). Swap roles for the second message.
exit_html: Each student submits: one real-feeling message they wrote + the tactics it uses + the correct defensive action.
